TEST DATA: for START TEST runs only. Never used for a real channel or upload.
Title (locked): Why Your Toilet Keeps Running, and How to Fix it
Channel: TEST Plumbing (no niche pack: every live fact re-checked before each script)
Verified on: 2026-10-19
Promise in plain words: A toilet that keeps running is usually one of three things in the tank: a flapper that isn't sealing, a water level set so high it spills into the overflow tube, or a fill valve that won't shut off. Tell which one you have, then fix it yourself for a few dollars.
Title claims -> support:
- "Keeps running" = both kinds (refills by itself every few minutes, OR never stops) -> F1 (flapper leak makes the fill valve switch back on) and F2 (float set too high, debris, or a failed valve keeps water flowing).
- "Why" -> F1, F2, F3 (two manufacturers name the same causes).
- "How to fix it" -> STEPS 1-9 give each cause a DIY fix; parts prices P1-P3.
- Brief's "almost always one of three": no source gives a share. Korky says "in most cases" for the flapper and lists the fill-valve causes (F1-F2). Honest wording: "most of the time." (See GAPS.)
- Brief's "tell which in a few minutes": the overflow check is instant, but the flapper tests take 10-25 minutes (F6-F8). Honest wording: "within about 15 minutes." (See GAPS.)

FACTS
- F1. "In most cases, a worn toilet flapper or flush valve seal is allowing water to slowly leak from the tank into the bowl. As the water level inside the tank drops, the fill valve float also drops and turns the water back on." | Korky, How to Fix a Running Toilet | https://www.korky.com/toilet-repair-help/running-toilet | 2026-10-19 | timeless
- F2. "If water continues flowing after the tank is full, the fill valve float may be set too high, clogged with debris, or failing to shut off. Adjusting, cleaning, or replacing the fill valve will fix a constantly running toilet." | Korky (same page) | https://www.korky.com/toilet-repair-help/running-toilet | 2026-10-19 | timeless
- F3. Fluidmaster's first check: with the water on, look in the tank to "determine if the water level is rising so high it is draining into the overflow pipe." If it is, clean the fill valve. If that fails, replace the fill valve. | Fluidmaster, Toilet Running Constantly | https://www.fluidmaster.com/toilet-problems/toilet-running-constantly/ | 2026-10-19 | timeless
- F4. Correct tank level: "roughly ½ inch below top of overflow pipe to ensure a proper flush. (Does not need to be exact.)" | Fluidmaster 400H PerforMAX installation instructions | https://fluidmaster.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/11/PerforMAX_2.0_Instructions_092818.pdf | 2026-10-19 | timeless
- F5. Korky agrees: set the valve so its water level mark "sits about 1/2" below the top of the flush valve overflow tube." A valve set too high "won't shut off, and you run the risk of the valve constantly running or overflowing." | Korky, How to Replace Toilet Fill Valve | https://www.korky.com/toilet-repair-help/how-to-replace-toilet-fill-valve | 2026-10-19 | timeless
- F6. Flapper test (Fluidmaster): turn off the water with the tank full, mark the level, and wait 10-15 minutes. If the level drops, "replace the flapper first as this is the most common problem." | Fluidmaster (F3 page) | https://www.fluidmaster.com/toilet-problems/toilet-running-constantly/ | 2026-10-19 | timeless
- F7. Flapper test (Korky): mark the level in pencil, turn off the supply, and wait "at least 25 minutes." If the level drops to the flapper, replace the flapper or seal. If it drops to a point on the overflow tube or to the bottom of the tank, replace the flush valve. | Korky (F1 page) | https://www.korky.com/toilet-repair-help/running-toilet | 2026-10-19 | timeless
- F8. Dye test: "placing a few drops of food coloring in the toilet tank. If any color shows up in the bowl after 10 minutes, you have a leak. (Be sure to flush immediately after the experiment to avoid staining the tank.)" | EPA WaterSense, Fix a Leak Week (page last updated March 13, 2026) | https://www.epa.gov/watersense/fix-leak-week | 2026-10-19 | timeless. (NYC DEP says wait 15-20 minutes and "the sooner the color appears, the larger the leak": W3 link.)
- F9. Chain slack: Korky says leave "1 to 2 chain links in slack." Too tight, and the flapper can't seal. Too loose, and links can fall under it. Fluidmaster's 400H sheet says "approximately 1/2" of slack." | Korky (F1 page) and Fluidmaster (F4 PDF) | links above | 2026-10-19 | timeless
- F10. Seat: "Inspect the flush valve sealing surface for debris buildup, mineral deposits, or visible damage. If mineral deposits are present, clean the drain opening so the flapper can seal." If it is cracked or warped, replace the flush valve. | Korky (F1 page) | https://www.korky.com/toilet-repair-help/running-toilet | 2026-10-19 | timeless
- F11. Flapper size: flappers come in 2" and 3" sizes (Fluidmaster recommends its 502 for 2"). EPA: "Bring the old flapper (or a picture of it) to the hardware store." | Fluidmaster (F3 page); EPA (F8 page) | links above | 2026-10-19 | timeless
- F12. Wear: EPA says the flapper should be "checked periodically and replaced at least every five years." Korky says fill valves "typically have a lifespan of 5-7 years." | EPA (F8 page); Korky (F5 page) | links above | 2026-10-19 | timeless
- F13. Old float-ball valves: "Do not replace an old fill valve that has a float ball with a new fill valve that has a float ball. Instead, use a new piston-valve type fill valve." | NYC DEP brochure | W3 link | 2026-10-19 | timeless
- F14. Time: Bob Vila's flapper guide estimates "Working Time: 10 minutes, Total Time: 20 minutes, Skill Level: Beginner." Fluidmaster's own product page says the 400H "Installs in under 10 minutes." That is a manufacturer claim; say it as one. | https://www.bobvila.com/articles/how-to-replace-toilet-flapper/ ; https://fluidmaster.com/shop/product/400h-performax-fill-valve/ | 2026-10-19 | timeless

STEPS OR METHOD
1. Shut off the supply valve behind the toilet (clockwise), then lift off the lid and set it down somewhere safe. | lid on a towel, valve turning | safety: the lid is fragile (S2)
2. Look in the tank: is water running into the top of the overflow tube? Yes = a fill valve or level problem (go to 3). No = test the flapper (go to 6). | water trickling into the tube | F3; this check is instant
3. Lower the level. On a 400H-style valve, turn the adjustment screw counterclockwise to lower the float (clockwise raises it), then flush to reset. Aim for about ½" below the top of the overflow tube. | screwdriver on the adjustment screw, level line vs. tube top | F4. Option: older valves differ (F13)
4. Still filling into the tube? Flush the debris out. Water off, then flush. Hold the float up, twist the cap and arm counterclockwise 1/8 turn and lift it off. Hold a cup upside down over the open valve and turn the water on "full force for 10-15 seconds." Check for debris, then put the cap back on. | cup over the uncapped valve | source: Fluidmaster F3 page (the 400H sheet says turn the water "on and off a few times"). Mistake: skipping the cup, which sprays water
5. Still runs after cleaning? Replace the fill valve. | new valve, height set ½" mark | F3, F5; price P2/P3. Hand-tighten only (S3)
6. Flapper test: mark the water line in pencil, shut off the supply and wait (F6/F7), or do the dye test (F8). | pencil line; blue water in bowl | flush right after the dye test (F8)
7. Level dropped? Check the chain first (1-2 links of slack). | chain hanging with slight slack | free fix (F9)
8. Clean any mineral crust off the flush valve seat where the flapper lands. | flapper lifted, rim of the drain opening | free fix (F10)
9. Still leaking? Replace the flapper with the same size (2" or 3"). If it still drains after a new flapper, the flush valve itself is the problem. That is a bigger job, outside this video's promise. | old flapper unhooked from its ears | F7, F11; price P1

- S1. Shut off the supply first: "turn off the water supply by turning the handle clockwise until the valve is fully closed." | Korky, How to Replace a Toilet Flapper | https://www.korky.com/toilet-repair-help/how-to-replace-toilet-flapper | 2026-10-19
- S2. "The lid is fragile. Place it somewhere safe. These lids aren't always available as individual parts, especially with older toilets. If it breaks, you may need to replace the entire toilet." | The Home Depot, How To Fix a Running Toilet | https://www.homedepot.com/c/ah/how-to-fix-a-running-toilet/9ba683603be9fa5395fab90138bd8691 | 2026-10-19
- S3. "Hand-tighten only. DO NOT OVER TIGHTEN." "Over tightening may crack the fill valve or tank causing flooding." | Fluidmaster 400H instructions (F4 link) | 2026-10-19
- S4. No bleach or chlorine drop-in tank cleaners: they "RESULT IN DAMAGE to tank components and MAY CAUSE FLOODING." | Fluidmaster 400H instructions (F4 link) | 2026-10-19
- S5. If the toilet keeps running and there's water on the floor, "immediately turn off water." | Fluidmaster (F3 page) | 2026-10-19

DOUBTER
- Objection, from real comments on Roger Wakefield's "How to Fix A Running Toilet GUARANTEED" (UV-peiKW9gM, 5.7M views, pulled 2026-10-19). One: "I followed along & mine is still running. So now I guess I need to replace that entire fill valve system??" (@ronnismith5672). Another: "every 5 minutes I hear a 4 second burst of water from that tube into the overflow pipe" (@BasedBullShark).
- What answers it: don't buy parts first. Run the checks in order to find which of the three it is (Fluidmaster's sequence, F3/F6). A toilet that refills in short bursts is losing water past the flapper (F1), so a new fill valve won't fix it. Do the free fixes first: lower the level, flush the debris, set the chain slack, clean the seat. Then buy only the part that failed: about $6.48 or $14.98 (P1/P2). Korky's own "still running after replacing the flapper?" list: wrong flapper size, chain length, dirty or damaged seat (F9-F11).
